results.evidence: rope_length_m, rack, rope_note and rope_type all describe a 30 m glacier rope per team; a published trip report of the traverse describes carrying a 30 m glacier rope with one picket each. No source calls for a 50-60 m rope on this route.

results.evidence: The Mountaineers route summary (via search) says the traverse is best in early season, April or May, before brush fills the gullies. The Mountain Project route description reports an early-June ascent with thin snow and gives no recommended window. Only one source states a best window, so neither June nor April-May is settled by two agreeing sources.

Mountain Project grades the traverse Easy 5th with 'Mod. Snow'; The Mountaineers grade it Grade III, 5.4, AI2 (snow). Neither supports AI3, and every descriptive field on the row describes moderate-to-steep snow, not ice pitches. AI2 is the highest figure either source gives and is consistent with moderate/steep snow.

The Mountain Project description mentions a bivy near 5,500 ft, implying a multi-day outing, but no source found states car-to-car or per-section hours for the traverse, so the 12 h PUBLISHED TIMES vs the two-day itinerary cannot be settled from outside sources.

Forest Service pages for the Brothers Trail #821, Lena Lake/Brothers Trailhead and Lena Lake Campground require only a recreation pass and say wilderness regulations apply, without mentioning any self-issue wilderness permit. A campground aggregator claims permits are needed beyond Lena Lake into The Brothers Wilderness. No two sources explicitly agree either way.

Two genuine camps: the ~3,000 ft forest climbers' camp and the terraces near 5,500 ft, which pitch_detail labels a possible bivy (Mountain Project also mentions a bivy near 5,500 ft); the descent text refers to the latter.

dist_km is the one-way figure; 14.5 km (~9 mi) one way is plausible for camp (~6 mi) plus the climb to the ridge, so distance is not a contradiction. gain_ft 6,042 is below the trailhead-to-summit net rise, but no outside source states a car-to-car gain for the traverse, so it cannot be changed.

The Mountaineers route summary (via search) says the Hourglass is reached at approximately 5,800 ft; an independent 2018 trip report says the party reached the Hourglass at 5,800 ft. No source places it at 6,200 ft.

A 2025 ski-ascent report finds the climbers' camp around 2,900 ft; a route summary returned by search describes a climbers' camp at 3,000 ft in the upper Valley of the Silent Men. approach, approach_variants and bivy (914 m) agree. The itinerary day-1 note (~3,600 ft) is left unchanged because its gainFt (2,900 from a 700 ft trailhead) is built on it and may describe the separate upper camp; changing it would create a new mismatch.

results.evidence: Multiple April ascents are documented (an April 14 ski ascent, an April 2020 trip report, an April 2026 report) and May snow ascents (2002, 2025); snow-free scrambling is reported from late August. The season chip starting in June excludes the documented spring window that best_season and approach_variants call primary.

One route map describes 3 miles to Lena Lake plus 2.8 miles through the Valley of the Silent Men to the campsites; a 2018 trip report gives about 3 miles to the lake plus about 2 miles up the East Fork to camp; a route summary gives about 5-6 miles. None supports 7 miles to camp.

Forest Service pages for the Brothers Trail, trailhead and Lena Lake require a recreation pass and say wilderness regulations apply, but do not mention a self-issue wilderness permit either way; one aggregator claims permits are needed beyond Lena Lake. No two sources explicitly settle it.
